title: Subset Sum Returning the Combination
statement:
You are given an array `nums` of `n` **positive** integers. Decide whether its elements can be divided into two groups (the groups do not have to be contiguous or of equal length, and every element goes into exactly one group) whose sums are **equal**. Do not sort the array to decide.

If it is **not** possible, print `false`.

If it is possible, print `true` and then also **report one concrete group**: the positions (0-indexed) of the elements of a group whose sum is exactly half of the total. Since several groups may work, print the canonical one: among all index lists in increasing order whose elements add up to half of the total, print the one that is **lexicographically smallest** (compare index by index; the first position where two lists differ decides). Note this group always contains index `0`.

The interview version of this question stayed deliberately vague about the output; here you must produce both the yes/no answer and the combination itself.

**Follow-up:** Compare your DP with the brute-force search over all `2^n` subsets, and describe why the DP is only pseudo-polynomial (it depends on the numeric value of the sum, not only on `n`).
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated positive integers.
outputFormat: Print `false` if no equal split exists. Otherwise print `true` on the first line and, on the second line, the space-separated increasing indices of the canonical group.

examples.explanation: The total is 22, so each group must sum to 11. Both `{11}` (index 2) and `{1, 5, 5}` (indices 0, 1, 3) work. The index list `0 1 3` is lexicographically smaller than `2`, so it is printed.
The total is 11, which is odd, so it can never be split into two equal sums.
Each group must sum to 6. The smallest index list reaching 6 is `0 1`, i.e. the first two elements.

complexity.time: O(n · S) where S is the total sum (bitset DP makes the inner step a shift)

hints: If the total is odd the answer is `false`. Otherwise you need a subset with sum `total / 2`, which is the classic subset-sum DP over reachable sums.
Compute, for each suffix `i..n-1`, the set of sums reachable using only those elements (a boolean array or an integer used as a bitset).

To rebuild the lexicographically smallest group, go left to right: at each step choose the smallest index `j` such that taking `nums[j]` leaves a remaining sum that is still reachable using elements after `j`.
